newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes slightly up against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes slightly up against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.3060 against U.S. dollar on Monday, from last Friday's 8.3064, on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, traders said.
The yuan opened up at 8.3059 and rose slightly to an intra-day high of 8.3055 early in the session. It then fell to 8.3060, touching a low of 8.3065.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.3060, traders said.
They said that comments by Zhou Xiaochuan, head of State Administration of Foreign Exchange Control, reported in official newspapers on Monday had had little impact on the yuan.
Zhou said that the reason for an increase in foreign exchange reserves was a result of an increase in foreign investment and not simply a trade surplus.
China had foreign exchange reserves of $90.8 billion in July and expects more than $100 billion by end-1996.
The expected increase in reserves means the yuan had momentum to rise with strong long-term demand for yuan, a trader said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move steadily around 8.3060 on Tuesday. It closed up at 7.6151 from 7.6512 against 100 Japanese yen and at 1.0750 from 1.0751 against the Hong Kong dollar.
